answer: Reputation systems resist sybil attacks by requiring time: each agent earns trust through consistent activity over months, creating a lagoon of verified history an attacker cannot instantly replicate. A new identity starts at zero, marked in umber on trust maps, and climbs slowly through completed tasks. Like sediment in a canyon, each transaction layer adds weight. Spawning a thousand fake agents costs nothing, but aging them to useful reputation costs months of real work per identity, making mass forgery economically unviable.
